_comment: Marketing platform IDs for Wagvive. These are PUBLIC identifiers: the GA4
measurement ID appears in the page source of every page, and the Merchant
Center ID is visible to anyone who inspects the feed. Safe to commit.
API keys, access tokens and secrets do NOT belong here. Those go in
config/*.env, which is gitignored. If a platform later needs a secret for
reporting (Google Ads developer token, Meta system user token), add it to
an env file and reference it by name here, never the value.
Owner account for all marketing platforms: OWNER_MARKETING_INBOX
(the dedicated store Gmail behind hello@wagvive.com forwarding, chosen so
the business can be handed over without handing over a personal account).

google.paid_campaigns: deliberately NOT enabled: Performance Max needs 30 to 50 conversions a month to learn and wastes budget below roughly $3,000/month. Google paid is phase 3, gated behind a 1.5% site conversion rate. See docs/marketing-plan-2026-08.md section 3.3.
google.data_retention: set to 14 months, the free-tier maximum. Not retroactive.
google.verified_live: 2026-08-06: confirmed two hits to google-analytics.com/g/collect with tid=G-W6EC4B37P0, gtag present, page_view sending to both G-W6EC4B37P0 and MC-9SXHKYQZTW. Domain verification meta tag present.
google.verify_command: load wagvive.com in a browser and run performance.getEntriesByType('resource') filtered for google-analytics; presence in page HTML alone does NOT prove the tag fires, because Shopify loads pixels in a sandbox

meta.status: pixel live; AD ACCOUNT RESTRICTED, review requested
meta.capi: data sharing set to Maximum in the Shopify app; server-side events cannot be verified from the browser, confirm in Events Manager that Purchase shows a server source
meta.verified_live: 2026-08-06: fbevents.js loaded, config fetched for 1770353747621287 with domain=wagvive.com, and a PageView sent to facebook.com/tr/. Transmission confirmed, not just configuration.
meta.ad_account_restriction: On creating the business portfolio Meta returned "Business Account Not Allowed to Advertise". Almost certainly automated risk scoring: the account had zero ad history, so there was nothing to violate. Review requested. DO NOT create a second portfolio or Facebook account: Meta links by device, IP and payment method and treats duplicates as ban evasion, which turns a temporary flag permanent. Not blocking, because Meta is phase 3 in the marketing plan and pixel collection is unaffected.
meta.if_review_fails: Pinterest is phase 1 anyway and unaffected. Revisit Meta after the business is an LLC with a business bank account, which clears these flags far more reliably than an individual account.

pinterest.status: tag installed as a Shopify web pixel; transmission to be confirmed in Pinterest tag health
pinterest.why_it_looks_broken: A STRICT web pixel runs inside Shopify's sandboxed iframe, so window.pintrk is undefined on the main page and its network calls never appear in the main document's performance resource list. This is expected and is NOT evidence of a broken tag. GA4 and Meta happen to load in the main page context, which is why the same check worked for them.
pinterest.how_to_verify: Pinterest Ads > Conversions > Tag health. It reports whether events are arriving and the time of the last one. There is no way to confirm a STRICT pixel from the storefront DOM.
pinterest.catalog: confirm catalog sync is ON. Product Pins are free organic distribution, the Pinterest equivalent of Google free listings, and the second zero-CPC channel in the plan.
pinterest.note: Phase 1 destination. At about $0.35 a click it is the only channel under our CAC ceiling on day one: the best offer supports a $0.43 click at a realistic 1% conversion rate.

tiktok.status: closed as not viable for TikTok SHOP (overseas direct shipping restricted, ~6 business day delivery requirement, ~30% all-in take). TikTok as an ads or organic channel to our own site remains open.
